maturity_tiers.Advanced: SBTi validated + CDP A/A- + full reporting + net zero target
maturity_tiers.Good: SBTi validated or committed + ISO 14001 + sustainability report
maturity_tiers.Progressing: Some credentials (ISO 14001 or report) but SBTi pending
maturity_tiers.Developing: Limited formal credentials; ESG reporting under development
maturity_tiers.Early Stage: Only basic certifications (e.g. ISO 14001); no SBTi / CDP

ArcelorMittal Europe.revenue: US$61.4B (ArcelorMittal Group sales, 2025); Europe segment US$28.8B
ArcelorMittal Europe.ownership: Listed — NYSE, Euronext Amsterdam/Paris, Luxembourg, Spanish exchanges (MT)
ArcelorMittal Europe.countries: Steelmaking in 14 countries; sales in ~126 countries
ArcelorMittal Europe.report: ArcelorMittal publishes an annual Sustainability Report (2025 edition under NFRD, GRI-referenced, with IFRS S1/S2 and SASB index and EY assurance on selected KPIs). Its SBTi commitment was removed in 2024 and the 2030 goal was cut from -25% to up to -10% Scope 1+2 intensity vs 2018, while a net-zero 2050 ambition is maintained. 95% of steel sites are ISO 14001 certified and 42 sites hold ResponsibleSteel certification; EAF output is ~26% of production. A large EPD library (IBU, Environdec, ITB) covers standard and XCarb low-carbon steels.

Buzzi Unicem.report: Buzzi holds an SBTi-validated near-term target (2023, well-below 2°C) to cut gross Scope 1+2 emissions 21.2% per tonne of cementitious product by 2030 vs 2021, within a GCCA-aligned 'Our Journey to Net Zero' roadmap targeting net zero by 2050 (net Scope 1 at 551 kg CO2/t in 2025 vs a <500 kg 2030 target). Since FY2024 it publishes an ESRS consolidated sustainability statement with limited assurance, including a full Scope 1-3 inventory, TCFD-based climate risk analysis and a 74.8% clinker/cement ratio. CCUS work includes the CI4C oxyfuel demonstrator and a potential capture plant at Deuna (Germany). Italian cements carry plant-specific EPDs under EPDItaly; the last public CDP score is B (2023).

Ceramica Imola.report: Ceramica Imola is part of the SACMI cooperative group. ISO 14001 certified. Publishes EPDs for its tile products. No SBTi or CDP participation confirmed.

Fassa Bortolo.report: Fassa Bortolo is a family-owned Italian manufacturer of premixed plasters, mortars, lime, paints and Gypsotech plasterboard (21 plants, 7 countries, €681M revenue in 2024). It publishes an annual sustainability report prepared with reference to GRI Standards 2021, disclosing Scope 1 and Scope 2 emissions (about 0.62 MtCO2e, dominated by lime-calcination process CO2) but no quantified Scope 3. ISO 14001 covers only selected sites (Botticino, Impa); the company runs an SGS-certified EPD Process with 21 EPDs published on Environdec. No SBTi, CDP or EcoVadis participation found.

Feralpi Group.countries: 7 (Italy, Germany, France, Spain, Czech Republic, Hungary, Algeria)
Feralpi Group.report: Feralpi is an EAF steelmaker (at least 98.6% recycled/recovered input) whose 2030 targets (-50% Scope 1-2-3 core-boundary intensity, -25% absolute non-core Scope 3 vs 2022) were approved by SBTi in 2024, followed by SBTi validation of net-zero 2050 targets in mid-2026. Its 2025 Integrated Report follows ESRS voluntarily, with EY limited assurance, and reports 56% renewable energy. Main plants hold ISO 14001, ISO 50001 and EMAS, and the group publishes about 21 EPDs, mostly on the International EPD System. No CDP or EcoVadis rating was found.

Florim.ownership: Private — Lucchese family (FinFloor S.p.A.); Società Benefit
Florim.countries: Production in Italy and USA; subsidiaries/flagships in UK, Korea and other markets
Florim.report: Florim was the world's first ceramic B Corp (2020) and was recertified in 2025 with 105.6 points; it is an Italian Società Benefit whose bylaws include a net-zero commitment. All plants hold ISO 14001, plus ISO 50001 and ISO 45001; products carry a company EPD (EPDItaly, EPDITALY0462), the Confindustria Ceramica sector EPD, HPDs and Declare Red List Free labels. Since 2024 it reports voluntarily on an ESRS basis (2025: 18th edition), disclosing Scope 1-2 (~296 kt CO2e in 2024) but omitting Scope 3; renewables are only 3.6% of total energy and there is no SBTi, CDP or EcoVadis rating.

Geberit.countries: Sales companies in 52 countries, products sold in 120+; 26 production plants
Geberit.report: Geberit's 2025 sustainability report, part of the Annual Report, is prepared in accordance with GRI and TCFD. It is structured on ESRS for the first time, with full CSRD/ESRS coverage planned from 2027. It reports Scope 1+2 of 108,446 t CO2e with limited assurance, and full Scope 3 of about 996 kt. The CO2 strategy targets -5% CO2 intensity per year and follows Switzerland's net-zero-2050 goal, but there is no SBTi-validated target, and CDP scored Geberit B in 2024 and 2025. Geberit holds EcoVadis Gold (2025) and a group ISO 9001/14001/45001 certificate, and publishes 32 EPDs on EPD Hub that cover about 44% of sales.

Gyproc.report: Gyproc is a brand of Saint-Gobain, which has been a Science Based Targets initiative leader since 2018 with a CDP A rating in 2024. The group targets net-zero by 2050 with a 2030 interim goal of -33% Scope 1+2 and -16% Scope 3. All gypsum products carry EPD declarations and the group reports under CSRD/ESRS from FY2024.

Heidelberg Materials.report: Heidelberg Materials has SBTi-validated 1.5°C near-term and net-zero targets (-26.7% gross Scope 1+2 per t cementitious and -25% absolute Scope 3 purchased goods by 2030 vs 2020; net zero 2050), scored CDP A for climate in 2025 and 74 in EcoVadis. Its 2025 Annual and Sustainability Report is the first prepared under ESRS (limited assurance) and includes TCFD/IFRS S2 disclosures; net Scope 1 fell to 512 kg CO2/t with a ~68% clinker ratio. It opened the cement industry's first industrial-scale CCS plant at Brevik (about 400 kt CO2/yr, evoZero) and is developing further CCUS projects including DREAM CCS at Rezzato-Mazzano (Italy). The Italian arm (ex Italcementi) publishes about 40 EPDs under the International EPD System, and its Italian plants are ISO 14001-certified.

Hilti.report: Hilti has validated SBTi targets and achieves CDP A- / B ratings. The company targets net-zero by 2050 with near-term milestones of -50% Scope 1+2 by 2030 and active Scope 3 engagement. Annual sustainability reports are GRI-aligned. ISO 14001 globally certified.

Holcim.report: Following the 2025 spin-off of its North American business as Amrize, Holcim restated its SBTi-validated 2030 and 2050 net-zero targets (Scopes 1-3, 2020 baseline). It received CDP A scores for Climate and Water in 2025. Its 2025 Sustainability Statement is prepared under ESRS and the Swiss Code of Obligations with EY assurance, disclosing 52 Mt Scope 1, 3 Mt Scope 2 and 37 Mt Scope 3 emissions; full CSRD compliance is targeted for 2027. 98% of cement sites are ISO 14001 certified.

Ideal Standard.report: Ideal Standard published its 2023 Sustainability Report ('Together for a better future'), reporting a 5% reduction in company-wide CO₂ (5,514 tonnes), removal of 41.5 tonnes of single-use plastic from packaging, and publication of 5,000 EPDs. The Wittlich (Germany) fittings plant achieved zero Scope 2 emissions with 100% renewable electricity. Ideal Standard received an EcoVadis Silver Medal (2023) — placing it in the top 25% of 85,000+ rated companies with its environmental performance rated 'advanced'. No SBTi or CDP confirmed as of Feb 2026.

Isover (Saint Gobain).report: (see Gyproc — all Saint-Gobain brands share group credentials)

James Hardie Europe GmbH.report: James Hardie Industries is listed on NYSE and publishes annual ESG reports. ISO 14001 is maintained at manufacturing plants. The company discloses Scope 1+2 emissions but SBTi and CDP participation status is not confirmed for the European operations specifically.

Kerakoll.report: Kerakoll is a certified B Corp (2023) and Italian Società Benefit (2021). Its 2024 Sustainability Report, prepared in accordance with GRI Standards but not externally assured, discloses Scope 1, 2 and full 15-category Scope 3 emissions (~716 ktCO2e total, 98% Scope 3). Italian plants hold ISO 14001, ISO 45001 and ISO 50001 (2024) and use 100% GO-certified renewable electricity; 70 new EPDs were published in 2024. EcoVadis is used to rate suppliers covering over half of COGS; no SBTi, CDP or net-zero commitment was found.

Knauf.report: Knauf Group has set internal 2032 targets (-50% absolute Scope 1+2 and -30% Scope 3 vs 2021, zero waste to disposal, no 'Red List' chemicals) and a 2045 net-zero ambition. None of these is SBTi-validated at group level, and there is no public group sustainability report. Disclosure comes from divisions and countries: Knauf Insulation reports Scope 1-3 and a CDP B (2024), and Knauf Italia publishes an ESRS-based 2024 sustainability report. Knauf Italia also holds ICMQ ISO 14001 certificates and C2C Silver for all Castellina plasterboards.

Laminam.ownership: Private equity — controlled by Alpha Private Equity Fund 7, with a stake held by CEO Alberto Selmi
Laminam.countries: Plants in Italy (Fiorano Modenese, Borgo Val di Taro) and Russia; sales in 100+ countries
Laminam.report: Laminam publishes an annual sustainability report (2025 edition released May 2026). It is voluntarily structured on ESRS and has no external assurance. Group Scope 1-2 emissions were 60.7 kt CO2e in 2025 (location-based); Scope 3 is not reported, and there is no SBTi, CDP or net-zero target. It holds ISO 9001, ISO 14001, ISO 20400 (sustainable procurement) and an ISO 14064-1 GHG verification, is part of the Confindustria Ceramica sector EPD, and reports product EPDs, HPD, CAM compliance and 20-60% recycled content.

Leca.report: (see Gyproc / Isover — Leca is a Saint-Gobain brand)

Marazzi.hq: Sassuolo (MO), Italy (Marazzi Group) / Calhoun GA, USA (Mohawk Industries)
Marazzi.revenue: ~$10.8B (Mohawk Industries Group, 2025); Marazzi is part of the Global Ceramic segment
Marazzi.ownership: Subsidiary of Mohawk Industries - listed NYSE (MHK)
Marazzi.report: Marazzi is part of Mohawk Industries. Mohawk's 2025 Impact Report (17th edition) comes with a GRI index, ISSB/SASB and TCFD disclosures, a CDP submission and a GHG statement showing Scope 1+2 of 2.58 Mt CO2e, which is not externally assured. Mohawk has no SBTi target (only Unilin is validated) and no net-zero goal; its new target is -20% Scope 1+2 by 2030 vs 2021. CDP scored Mohawk B in 2024 and 'Not Scored' in 2025. Marazzi holds ISO 9001/14001/45001/50001 and ISO 17889-1 certificates and an EcoVadis Bronze medal. Its Italian EPDItaly EPDs have expired; the active Environdec EPDs cover the Daltile-owned Marazzi USA/Mexico range.

Metra.ownership: Private equity — KPS Capital Partners (75%) via Fengari Holding I B.V.
Metra.countries: 45 (client base); plants in Italy, USA, Canada
Metra.parent: Fengari Holding I B.V. (KPS Capital Partners)
Metra.report: Metra is an Italian vertically integrated aluminium group (foundry, extrusion, finishing, window and façade systems) controlled 75% by KPS Capital Partners through the Dutch Fengari holding. Its Rodengo Saiano foundry and extrusion site is ASI Performance Standard V3.1 certified (valid to 2028) and holds ISO 14001 and ISO 45001; the RE.AL.E low-carbon billet range contains up to 100% pre-consumer recycled aluminium and is covered by an EPD Italy EPD, alongside a curtain-wall EPD. The first group Sustainability Report 2024 (GRI with reference) discloses Scope 1, 2 and 8 Scope 3 categories (~1.55 MtCO2e, 98% purchased goods) and prepares for CSRD, but there is no SBTi target, CDP disclosure or EcoVadis rating.

Pittini.report: Pittini Group operates EAF steelmaking with high recycled scrap content. ISO 14001 certified. Annual sustainability report published. No SBTi or CDP participation confirmed.

Rockfon.report: (see Rockwool — Rockfon is a ROCKWOOL Group brand)

Rockwool.countries: 40 factories in 23 countries; sales in 120+ countries
Rockwool.report: ROCKWOOL Group holds SBTi-validated near-term targets (-38% absolute Scope 1+2 and -20% Scope 3 by 2034 vs 2019) and in 2025 formalised a net-zero 2050 commitment with a 1.5°C-aligned update to be submitted to SBTi in 2026. It scored A- in CDP Climate Change and Water (2025 cycle), and ROCKWOOL France holds EcoVadis Platinum (87/100). Sustainability reporting is an ESRS sustainability statement within the Annual Report, with limited assurance and a TCFD reference table; 74% of factories are ISO 14001 certified. Stone wool products are covered by factory-range EPDs on the International EPD System and EPD-Norge/EPD-Global, and the Rockcycle take-back service runs in 25 countries.

Schüco.report: Schüco publishes sustainability reports and participates in CDP. The company discloses Scope 1+2 emissions and targets carbon-neutral production by 2030. No confirmed SBTi validation. ISO 14001 is maintained at manufacturing sites.

Siniat.hq: Zaventem, Belgium (Etex NV); Siniat Italy: Assago (MI), plant in Corfinio (AQ)
Siniat.ownership: Private — Etex NV, family shareholders (not listed)
Siniat.report: Siniat is the plasterboard brand of Etex Building Performance (Etex Group). Etex's near-term targets (-58% absolute Scope 1+2 by 2032 vs 2019, -30% Scope 3 vs 2024) were approved by SBTi in August 2026, and the group holds an EcoVadis Silver medal (75/100). The 2025 Annual Report includes ESRS-aligned sustainability statements with full Scope 1-3 disclosure, and 81% of European turnover is covered by EPDs. In Italy the Corfinio plant is ISO 14001/9001/45001 certified and publishes 14 EPD Hub EPDs, ISO 14021 recycled-content claims and C2C Bronze plasterboards.

Ursa.report: URSA has been part of Etex since June 2022 (acquired from Xella). Climate and reporting credentials sit at Etex Group level: SBTi near-term targets validated on 20 Aug 2026 (Scope 1+2 -58.43% by 2032 vs 2019; Scope 3 -30% by 2032 vs 2024), EcoVadis Silver (top 9%), full Scope 1-3 disclosure and an ESRS-aligned sustainability statement ahead of CSRD. At URSA level, URSA Ibérica holds ISO 14001 (TÜV Rheinland, to 2027) and products carry EPDs (Environdec, IBU, ZAG, DAPc), EUCEB, Eurofins Indoor Air Comfort Gold and Blue Angel. In August 2026 Etex entered exclusive talks to sell URSA's XPS business (incl. Bondeno, IT) to Austrotherm.

Weber.report: (see Gyproc — Weber is a Saint-Gobain brand)

Wienerberger.report: Wienerberger is listed on the SBTi dashboard with a commitment to set near-term and net-zero targets (May 2025) but has no validated targets yet; its climate transition plan and 2030 targets are under revision. The group scores CDP B (2025) and MSCI AAA, held EcoVadis Gold (Nov 2024), and publishes an ESRS sustainability statement with limited assurance. Under its Sustainability Program 2023-2026 it has cut Scope 1+2 CO2 intensity by 20.7% vs 2020 (target -25%) and Scope 3 by 25.2% vs 2022, and about 50% of production sites are ISO 14001 certified. EPDs are published country by country across several programme operators (International EPD System, Bau-EPD, EPD Italy and UK EPDs).

Wurth.report: Würth participates in CDP and publishes annual sustainability reports. ISO 14001 is maintained. Scope 1+2 emissions are disclosed. SBTi commitment status is not confirmed as of 2026.

Xella Italia.report: Xella Group has validated SBTi targets for 42% reduction in Scope 1+2 by 2030. Annual sustainability reporting follows GRI. Xella Italia inherits all group-level credentials including CDP participation and ISO 14001 across production sites.

Celenit.report: Italian SME producing cement-bonded wood-wool insulation boards. EcoVadis Silver (Feb 2025; Gold in 2022), PEFC and FSC chain-of-custody certificates (ICILA), ANAB-ICEA, natureplus and Eurofins Indoor Air Comfort Gold, eight EPDs on the International EPD System (valid to 2030) and ISO 9001 (Certiquality). No SBTi, CDP, net-zero target, GHG inventory, sustainability report or ISO 14001 found.

Stiferite.report: Italian PIR insulation producer. ISO 9001, ISO 14001 (renewed to April 2029) and ISO 45001 certified by DNV. Thirteen valid IBU-verified EN 15804+A2 EPDs, ReMade in Italy certification (Bureau Veritas, valid to Nov 2027), a CAM compliance handbook for DM 24/11/2025 and Eurofins Indoor Air Comfort Gold. No SBTi, CDP, EcoVadis, GHG disclosure or sustainability report found.

Polisette.report: Family-owned Italian EPS producer (Polistar range). ISO 9001 (ICMQ, valid to Jan 2028), 13 EPD Italy EPDs (valid to Apr 2027), Plastica Seconda Vita (IIP, valid to Nov 2027), ReMade in Italy (ICMQ, certificates dated to expire June 2026) and a CAM declaration. The 2026 quality & environment policy announces an integrated ISO 14001 system, not yet certified. No SBTi, CDP, EcoVadis, GHG disclosure or sustainability report found.

EDILTEC.report: Italian PIR (POLIISO) and XPS (X-FOAM) producer, Ediltec Insulation S.p.A. (Gruppo SBN, group revenue >EUR 100M). ISO 9001 (SGS, valid to July 2027), 13 EPD Italy EPDs valid to 2029-2030 and the ANPE polyurethane mark; its SGS-verified recycled-content (CAM) certificate expired in 2023. No SBTi, CDP, EcoVadis, ISO 14001, GHG disclosure or sustainability report found.

Sedus.ownership: Private AG — Stoll VITA Stiftung 60.95%, Karl Bröcker Stiftung 32.45%
Sedus.countries: Production in Germany (Dogern, Geseke, Owingen/Klöber); sales in 70+ countries
Sedus.report: Foundation-owned, unlisted German office-furniture maker (HQ Dogern; plants in Dogern and Geseke; ~EUR 216M revenue 2025); Italian subsidiary Sedus Stoll S.r.l., Cadorago (CO). ISO 14001, ISO 50001, ISO 45001, SA8000 and EcoVadis Gold (Oct 2025); GRI Core sustainability reports (latest: 2023); EMAS discontinued in 2022. SBTi near-term and net-zero 'Commitment' (no validated targets) with a proprietary 2050 net-zero goal. Sites are 'climate compensated' since 1 Jan 2026 via offsets (Wilderness International); the -30% Scope 1 target slipped to 2026. Product credentials: FEMB level, Blauer Engel (22 products), GREENGUARD and self-declared EPI sheets (EN 15804 LCA); no third-party EPDs found.

Fellowes Italia.ownership: Private — Fellowes Leonardi S.p.A., subsidiary of Fellowes, Inc. (family-owned)
Fellowes Italia.countries: Group entities in 13 countries; products sold in 30+ countries
Fellowes Italia.report: Fellowes Leonardi S.p.A. is the Italian subsidiary of family-owned Fellowes, Inc. (Itasca, IL), operating from Camerano (AN) with registered office in Milan (~EUR 9.8M revenue, 15 employees, 2025). The group publishes an annual Impact Report with reference to GRI (2026 ed., CY2025 data, not assured): Scope 1 2,476 t, Scope 2 2,985 t (market-based), estimated Scope 3 ~276 kt CO2e; target -10% absolute Scope 1-3 by 2030 vs 2023, no SBTi commitment or net-zero goal. CDP participant since 2020 (score not public), EcoVadis Silver (Fellowes Europe, 2026), ISO 14001 at UK and Dutch sites (Italy: ISO 9001 only), FSC CoC in Europe, SCS Indoor Advantage Gold and BIFMA LEVEL product labels; no EPDs.

Sto Italia.ownership: Listed — Frankfurt/XETRA, SDAX (preference shares, ISIN DE0007274136)
Sto Italia.report: Sto Italia Srl is the Italian subsidiary (Empoli, FI) of the Sto Group, a facade specialist (StoTherm ETICS, renders, coatings), wholly owned since November 2022. The Group publishes a Sustainability Statement inside its annual report, prepared voluntarily to CSRD/ESRS for the second year and given limited assurance by PwC. No SBTi target: the transition plan states no absolute GHG cut is achievable by 2030 because of growth, with at least -90% absolute by 2050 against a 2024 base and climate neutrality 2050 under Regulation (EU) 2021/1119 — the pathway is built on the SBTi Net Zero Tool but is not SBTi-validated. 2025 GHG: Scope 1 28,212 tCO2e, market-based Scope 2 5,787, Scope 3 1,259,470 (total market-based 1,293,469, -15.0% vs 2024). Renewables are 20.7% of energy use. ISO 14001 covers 24 Group companies, ISO 50001 all production plants and ten subsidiaries, ISO 9001 28 of 32 plants. EPDs are published through several programme operators (IBU, Kiwa-Ecobility Experts, EPD-Global) and StoTherm Classic L MW carries the Blauer Engel ecolabel. No CDP score or EcoVadis rating found in public sources (October 2026).
